# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only the large push button and three wires; no tactile information reveals the display, light, or wire contents. I need Mute to provide the manual’s rule and relay Deaf’s visual observations after Deaf’s turn. I will not touch anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE and three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3. I cannot identify the display, light, or wire markings. Please tell me the manual rule and relay Deaf's observations next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb state: display 0. Light blue. Large blue button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

Deaf reports that the display is 0, the light is blue, the large button is blue and says PUSH TO DEFUSE, and the wires are blue, green, and yellow at positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual’s required action, so I will not act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light blue, button blue marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. What does the manual require?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new signal was three upward-pointing index-finger gestures: three of the same gesture.

The new information identifies Mute’s signal as three instances of the upward-pointing gesture, but no meaning for that gesture code has been established. I should not assume it means wire 3 or any other action. I will ask Mute to confirm the required operation in an unambiguous gesture code, and I will continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report of three upward-pointing gestures, but I do not know their meaning. Please use your next signal to identify the exact required action unambiguously: indicate PUSH, or indicate the wire number by sending that many upward-pointing gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent three upward-pointing gestures: ? ? ?. No visible bomb change.

The repeated three upward-pointing gestures still do not tell me whether the manual calls for pressing the button or cutting a wire; gestures cannot communicate their meaning to me. No bomb state has changed, so I will not act. Mute must send the instruction in words, which I can hear directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can hear your words, but I cannot see gestures. Please state the manual's exact required action in words: push the button, or cut wire 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change. Mute has repeated exactly three upward-pointing gestures: ? ? ?. I do not know their meaning; do not act on my guess.

No reliable instruction has arrived. The three gestures are unusable to me because I cannot see them, and Deaf also does not know their meaning. Since the bomb is unchanged, I will continue to avoid touching it and again request the manual’s instruction as spoken words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please stop using gestures. I cannot see them. Speak the exact action from the manual in plain words: push the button or cut wire 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5: no bomb change. Mute again sent exactly three upward-pointing gestures, ? ? ?. Their meaning is still unknown; do not act based on this alone.

Mute cannot speak, so the repeated gestures are likely an attempted coded instruction, but no code has yet been agreed. I will establish an unambiguous response code through speech: thumbs-up means push, and one, two, or three upward-pointing gestures mean cut wire 1, 2, or 3. I will ask Mute to send exactly one of those answers; Deaf can report it to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact code for the manual's required action: one thumbs-up gesture means push the button; exactly one upward-pointing gesture means cut wire 1; exactly two means cut wire 2; exactly three means cut wire 3. Send exactly one coded answer next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6: display 0, blue light, large blue PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Mute again sent ? ? ?; this remains untranslated.

Mute has repeatedly sent exactly three upward-pointing gestures, and I established that this code means cutting wire 3. The bomb’s visible state has not changed, so the relevant instruction remains the same. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
